title: How Agents Use Context Engineering
summary: LangChain's Lance on offload/reduce/isolate context principles across Claude Code, Manus and Deep Agents.

assertions.quote: the task length is doubling around every seven months

verdicts.note: METR's 2025 time-horizon study found ~7-month doubling (faster in 2024-25); later measurements stayed on or above trend, with wide error bars.

assertions.quote: performance degrades with respect to context length

verdicts.note: Long-context benchmarks (e.g. NoLiMa, context-rot studies) show degradation as context grows; the exact threshold is model-dependent.

assertions.quote: giving agents access to a file system is very useful. It lets agents save and recall information

verdicts.note: External notes/memory files are a standard, effective pattern (Anthropic, Manus write-ups) for long tasks; adds retrieval overhead.

assertions.quote: keeping the function calling layer very lightweight

verdicts.note: Tool-selection accuracy drops as tool count grows (e.g. Berkeley function-calling and RAG-MCP results); dynamic tool loadouts help.

assertions.quote: progressively disclosing actions ... without loading all that into the system prompt ahead of time

verdicts.note: Skills load only short descriptions until used, and deferred tool loading cuts context; this is how Claude Code, Manus and others manage large capability sets.

assertions.quote: when you do summarization you necessarily lose information

verdicts.note: Summarization cuts cost and keeps sessions going, but lossy summaries can drop details that matter; quality depends on what is kept.

assertions.quote: That sub aent has its own context window ... and just return the output back to the parent agent

verdicts.note: Subagents return summaries rather than raw exploration; Anthropic reports gains from multi-agent research, at higher token cost.
